**1B.5 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador in 2024**

I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that AMLO used nuclear capability to shield conventional aggression, territorial coercion, or domestic repression. The available 2024 record is instead about disarmament diplomacy, nuclear-weapon-free-zone commitments, and civilian nuclear safety at Laguna Verde. The only negative material I found concerns a civilian nuclear incident, not coercive nuclear shielding.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Mexico promotes peace at the eighth OPANAL course on nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-01-26 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-promotes-peace-at-the-eighth-opanal-course-on-nuclear-disarmament-and-non-proliferation?idiom=en | Mexico trained foreign affairs, defense, navy, and security officials on disarmament and nonproliferation. That points to compliance and restraint, not using nuclear capability as cover for coercion or repression. | 1B.5, 1B.4 |
| [Foreign Ministry prioritizes nuclear disarmament on Mexico’s international agenda](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-02-14 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/foreign-ministry-prioritizes-nuclear-disarmament-on-mexico-s-international-agenda?idiom=en | Mexico framed its diplomacy around a safer, more peaceful world grounded in law and cooperation rather than weapons. This is the opposite of nuclear shielding logic. | 1B.5, 1B.4, 1B.2 |
| [With World at Delicate Crossroads, Disarmament Committee’s Responsibility ‘Immense’, Says General Assembly President During Robust Debate](https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm) | United Nations, Meetings Coverage and Press Releases | 2024-10-08 | https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3737.doc.htm | Mexico’s representative urged fewer warheads, more disarmament, and less rhetoric threatening nuclear use. This supports a no-escalation, no-shield posture. | 1B.5, 1B.4, 1B.2 |
| [Mexico chairs OPANAL General Conference](https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-chairs-opanal-general-conference?idiom=en) | Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores | 2024-11-28 | https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-chairs-opanal-general-conference?idiom=en | Mexico reaffirmed commitment to the Treaty of Tlatelolco and a world free of nuclear weapons, while OPANAL participants reiterated disarmament and dialogue. This is strong anti-shield evidence. | 1B.5, 1B.4 |
| [NEWS: Declaration of Unusual Event (NUP-4.1)](https://www-news.iaea.org/ErfView.aspx?mId=cfd216c1-7b9d-4653-9e55-10b13e8da30d) | International Atomic Energy Agency | 2024-01-12 | https://www-news.iaea.org/ErfView.aspx?mId=cfd216c1-7b9d-4653-9e55-10b13e8da30d | Laguna Verde had a smoke/fire incident that the IAEA logged as an unusual event. This is negative nuclear-safety evidence, but it does not show nuclear capability being used to shield aggression, coercion, or repression. | 1B.5, 1B.3 |
| [Se agudizan las fallas en Laguna Verde durante este sexenio](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/periodismo-de-investigacion/se-agudizan-las-fallas-en-laguna-verde-durante-este-sexenio/) | El Universal | 2024-08-18 | https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/periodismo-de-investigacion/se-agudizan-las-fallas-en-laguna-verde-durante-este-sexenio/ | The investigation says the January fire lasted hours and the alarm response was inadequate. Again, this is operational-safety criticism, not evidence of coercive nuclear shielding. | 1B.5, 1B.3 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported reading: **AMLO did not use nuclear capability as a shield for aggression, territorial coercion, or domestic repression in 2024.**
- I found **positive evidence of restraint** through repeated disarmament and Tlatelolco/OPANAL commitments.
- I found **no direct counterevidence** of nuclear coercion, brinkmanship, or nuclear-backed repression.
- The only adverse nuclear-related evidence concerns **civilian safety at Laguna Verde**, which is relevant to nuclear governance but not to this specific coercion question.

**Search gap**

- The search is inherently thin because Mexico is a **non-nuclear-weapon state** and 2024 reporting centers on disarmament and civilian safety, not coercive nuclear posturing.
- No 2024 source surfaced showing Mexico possessed or threatened nuclear capability in a way that could shield conventional aggression, territorial coercion, or repression.
